title: PanNET vs adjacent pancreas
subtitle: 16 samples · bulk RNA-seq
description: Bulk RNA-seq of 10 pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors and 6 tumor-adjacent pancreas samples (Niedra et al., PLOS One 2025; GEO GSE281039), compared with Cellaris.
bannerText: Public bulk RNA-seq of 10 pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PanNETs) and 6 adjacent pancreas samples (GEO GSE281039), compared with Cellaris. The tumors lie outside the healthy pancreas reference, so this demo shows bulk-level comparisons and composition only.

pathways.themeCaveat: Themes that share hub genes (ribosomal proteins, histones, proteasome subunits) can be called from those shared genes alone. Hallmark and PROGENy sets are shown next to their best-matching sets from other databases.

composition.banner: These samples are not well described by the healthy human pancreas cell types of the built-in reference. Estimated fractions describe each sample as a mixture of healthy pancreas cell types only; cell types that the reference lacks (for example tumor cells) cannot be estimated and are absorbed into the nearest types.
composition.test: two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum per cell type; Benjamini-Hochberg across the nine types

sources.name: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor bulk RNA-seq
sources.citation: Niedra et al., PLOS One 2025 (CC BY 4.0)
sources.role: Comparison demo: 10 tumors, 6 adjacent pancreas samples

limitations: Tumor samples lie outside the healthy pancreas reference (8 of 10 flagged). Their estimated fractions describe them as mixtures of healthy pancreas cell types; tumor cells cannot be estimated and are absorbed into the nearest types.
Estimated single-cell profiles and cell-level pathway activity are not shown for tumor samples.
Differential expression and pathway enrichment use the bulk counts. They combine differences in composition with differences within cell types.
Five of the six adjacent samples come from patients whose tumors are also included; the comparison treats all samples as independent.
The samples are FFPE resections with many zero counts, so size factors were computed from positive counts.
For research use only. Not for diagnostic use.
